results.content: + How to search Grey literature for systematic reviews. ## What is grey literature? "The term ‘grey literature’ is often used to refer to reports published outside of traditional commercial publishing. Review authors should generally search sources such as dissertations and conference abstracts" (Higgins et al. Grey literature may include research reports, conference papers, dissertations and theses, clinical trials, government documents, census data, standards, patents, and other research outputs. * It is the only source of information- e.g. research data, letters and unpublished studies. * It overcomes, or minimises, reporting or publication biases; grey literature is more likely to include negative results - e.g. clinical trials. * It provides new information not yet published in traditional sources - e.g. conference papers. * It provides more local information - e.g. government reports, local collections. ## How to search Grey literature for systematic reviews. You may wish to include searches for preprints in your systematic review. In some literature databases in a specific field, e.g. PsycINFO, you can search for preprints. You can limit your search to a specific document type, e.g. conference object or report. In some literature databases, e.g. Web of Science and Scopus, you can search for conference proceedings. You can limit your search to a specific document type, e.g. conference object or report. ## Reporting grey literature searching. When you are writing up your review remember to report on any grey literature searching you have done. Please note that reproducibility is harder to achieve for grey literature searches, due to the frequency of changes to websites and search engines. Describe any online or print source purposefully searched or browsed (e.g., tables of contents, print conference proceedings, web sites) and how this was done. * “We also searched the grey literature using the search string: "public attitudes" AND "sharing" AND "health data" on Google (in June 2021). * “The grey literature search was conducted in October 2021 and included targeted, iterative hand searching of 22 government and/or research organization websites that were suggested during the expert consultation and are listed in S1 Protocol. Twenty two additional citations were added to the review from the grey literature search.”.

Protocol, Search Log and Review Protocol. - Updating Database Searches+ 1.9. + 1.11 Literature Searching and AI. * Courses - Literature Searching and Reviews. ## Reporting a search history. Why do you need reporting a search history? In a literature search, it is essential to achieve reproducibility, transparency and a high level of detail. The search should be reported by showing: Where you searched, what you searched for and how many results it returned. All searched databases and other sources of information should be reported. It is important that you include the date of each search - in each source. ## Reporting Guidelines - PRISMA 2020. PRISMA 2020 Statement (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses) is a reporting tool for use when preparing systematic reviews and includes a checklist and a flowchart. * PRISMA 2020 Checklist includes 27 items that should be reported when preparing a systematic review. * PRISMA for Protocols, related to reporting in connection with the creation of protocols for systematic reviews. * PRISMA for Scoping Reviews, related to the reporting in connection with the creation of scoping reviews. * PRISMA for Searching, which includes 16 points that should be reported in connection with literature searches for systematic reviews. ## Search History. Conduct a complete search in an Ovid database and in the end write ..ps in the search field and the search history is shown. ## Updating Database Searches. When creating reviews for publication, it may be appropriate to update the searches to include the latest literature. * McGill Library suggests that you run your saved searches again, exporting them as RIS files that you import into Covidence (which removes duplicates). You should adjust the PRISMA flowchart and report the date of the last search, etc. * Another option is to use the databases' field codes and time limits to update the search to that date. McGill Library has an overview of how to use search fields for the different databases. * A third option is by using Covidence, You ca see a description in the Covidence guidance ”How to update a review with new studies - Tracking study sources and update numbers”: .

results.content: Literature Search Strategies For Students 2025 | Database Research Guide. 4. Literature Search Strategies For Students 2025. Literature Search Strategies For Students 2025. research methods literature search database strategies academic databases source identification. Literature Search Strategies For Students 2025. Effective literature searching is the foundation of quality academic research, yet many students struggle with inefficient search strategies that waste time and miss crucial sources. In 2025, with the exponential growth of academic publications and the proliferation of databases, mastering systematic literature search techniques has become more critical than ever for research success. In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore 8 essential literature search strategies that will transform your research efficiency and help you identify the most relevant, high-quality sources for your academic work. Database selection significantly impacts the comprehensiveness and quality of your literature search. Boolean operators are the foundation of sophisticated database searching, allowing you to combine search terms logically to retrieve precisely targeted results. Subject headings and controlled vocabularies provide standardized terminology for indexing and searching academic literature. These tools ensure consistent retrieval regardless of the specific terms authors use, significantly improving search comprehensiveness and precision. Strategic use of search filters and limits helps manage large result sets and focuses searches on the most relevant and high-quality sources. Citation searching, also known as snowballing, leverages the interconnected nature of academic literature to discover additional relevant sources. ### Citation Searching Strategies:. * **Search terms:** Keywords and subject headings used. Mastering literature search strategies is essential for conducting rigorous academic research in 2025. ### How many databases should I search for a comprehensive literature review? If key papers don't appear in your results, refine your search terms. ### Should I use different search strategies for different databases? For example, use MeSH terms in PubMed, APA Thesaurus terms in PsycINFO, and adjust search syntax according to each database's Boolean operators and field searching capabilities. For too many results: add more specific terms with AND, use subject headings, apply filters, or search specific fields. Use region-specific databases (e.g., CNKI for Chinese literature), search with native language terms, consult with native speakers for appropriate terminology, and consider using translation tools for search terms.

results.content: # Scoping Reviews: Step 3: Conduct Literature Searches. + Search with controlled vocabulary and keywords. + Translate to other databases and other searching methods. * How to create a search strategy with Boolean operators, database-specific syntax, subject headings, and appropriate keywords. Librarians are experts trained in literature searching and scoping review methodology. Databases index various journals, so in order to be comprehensive, it is important to search multiple databases when conducting a scoping review. ## Search with controlled vocabulary and keywords. Instead, you are searching certain citation data fields, like title, abstract, keyword, controlled vocabulary terms, and more. When developing a literature search, a good place to start is to identify searchable concepts of the research question, and then expand by adding other terms to describe those concepts. Not all citations are indexed with controlled vocabulary terms, however, so it is important to combine controlled vocabulary searches with keyword, or text word, searches. Boolean operators are used to combine terms in literature searches. OR is used to combine search terms for the same concept (i.e., influenza vaccine). Field tags tell the database exactly where to search. For example, you can use a field tag to tell a database to search for a term in just the title, the title and abstract, and more. If you do not manually apply field tags to your search, most databases will automatically search in a set of citation data points. **For scoping review searching, best practice is to apply field tags to each term for reproducibility.**. For more information about how to use a variety of databases, check out our guides on searching. These commands tell databases exactly how to combine terms together, and if done incorrectly or inefficiently, search results returned may be too broad or irrelevant. ## Translate to other databases and other searching methods. ### Translating search strategies to other databases. Our sections on Controlled Vocabulary and Field Tags have information on how to build searches in different databases. There are several databases specific to grey literature that can be searched. At a minimum, document and report certain elements, such as databases searched, including name (i.e., Scopus) and platform (i.e. Elsevier), websites, registries, and grey literature searched.
